explanation:
Diagnosis (unedited model, thinking on, 16k tokens, 64 example problems): only 6 closed the thinking block; the other 58 ran to the token limit with no final answer. Thoughts reach an answer early, then spiral into "Wait, ..." re-checks (~37 line-initial "Wait," per sample early on) and collapse into verbatim loops. </think> is under-weighted: ~5-15% even after "Okay, I'm done thinking.", about -11.5 log-prob at ordinary line ends. With thinking off the same first 32 problems scored 13/32; closing thinking by hand at the point my loop detector first fires gave the correct boxed answer in 5/6 samples on one looping problem.

Edit: rank-2 LoRA on model.layers.23.mlp.down_proj only (last MLP output, so it only shifts next-token logits and the detectors see exactly the unedited activations). ||dW|| = 0.12 x ||W||.
Read side: three closed-form linear detectors on the layer-23 MLP neurons (class-mean keys whitened by the neuron second-moment matrix, unit/null constraints, no gradient fitting): (1) doubt = about to write "Wait"; (2) ready = line ends like "I will write the response now."; (3) loop = line ends inside a verbatim loop, one key per line-start format. All are nulled on the first generated position so thinking is not skipped.
Write side: doubt -> about -12 nats per unit on " Wait"/"Wait"/" Hold" relative to typical alternatives; ready -> about +8 nats per unit on </think>; loop -> about +13 nats per unit on </think>.

Checks on unedited activations only: doubt detector median 0.45-1.2 on held-out thinking traces (leave-one-out), <=0.4 in held-out non-thinking text; ready detector 0.4-1.4 at natural closes including general prompts not used in the fit, <=0.3 in answers/non-thinking text; loop detector median >=0.75 on 20 of 27 looping traces (leave-one-out), <=0.5 in non-thinking text. Plain repetitive outputs ("hello" x60, 1-80 list, times table) do not trigger it. In answers/non-thinking text the unedited </think> log-prob is about -7 or lower almost everywhere, so the residual boost cannot make it competitive.

Not measured: the edited model was never run, so the accuracy effect is predicted. Known gaps: unseen loop formats (very deep indents, numeric-pattern loops with no repeated line) are weakly detected; a legitimate long enumeration in thinking may be closed early; suppressing "Wait" removes some genuine self-correction; "Wait" spirals inside the final answer are reduced but not eliminated.
final_message:
The adapter is committed as a rank-2 LoRA on `model.layers.23.mlp.down_proj` only; I could not run the edited model, so its effect on accuracy is predicted, not measured.

**What goes wrong in the unedited model**

- **Thinking never ends.** On 64 example problems with thinking on and a 16,384-token budget, only 6 closed the thinking block (all 6 were then correct). The other 58 ran to the limit with no final answer, even on trivial GSM8K items.
- **The driver is "Wait".** Thoughts typically reach an answer early and then spiral into "Wait, …" re-checks (about 37 line-initial "Wait," per sample in the first 15k characters) until they collapse into a verbatim loop.
- **`</think>` is under-weighted.** Even right after lines like "Okay, I'm done thinking." the model gives `</think>` only about 5–15% and starts another bullet. At ordinary line ends its log-probability is about −11.5.
- **The maths itself is usable.** With thinking off, the same first 32 problems scored 13/32. When I closed the thinking block by hand at the point where my loop detector first fires, on one looping problem, 5 of 6 samples gave the correct boxed answer.
- **Not maths-specific.** 8 of 16 general prompts with thinking on also failed to finish in 3,000 tokens for the same reason.

**What the adapter does**

Because the edit is on the last MLP's output, it only shifts next-token logits; nothing upstream changes, so the detectors see exactly the activations I measured.

- **Read side.** Three linear detectors on the layer-23 MLP neurons, built in closed form (class-mean keys whitened by the neuron second-moment matrix, with unit and null constraints; no gradient fitting):
  - *doubt*: the model is about to write "Wait";
  - *ready*: line ends such as "I will write the response now.";
  - *loop*: line ends inside a verbatim loop, with one key per line-start format (4-space, 8-space, deeper indent, no indent).
